title: What is shared, and what is atomic

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the JMM specification promise about a plain (non-volatile) `long` field that one thread writes while another reads it?

options.text: A 64-bit write may be split in two, so a read can mix two values
options.says: The page's Q5 answer says JLS 17.7 does not require non-volatile long and double writes to be atomic, so a reader may see half of each value.

options.text: A 64-bit write happens in one step, so a read sees one whole value
options.says: The page says 64-bit JVMs usually behave this way but the specification does NOT guarantee it for a plain long.

options.text: A 64-bit write is delayed until a lock is released by the writer
options.says: The page ties no plain write to a lock release; it names volatile long or AtomicLong as the fix for split writes.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does declaring a shared `int[]` field `volatile` give its readers?

options.text: Volatile reads and writes of the reference and every element
options.says: The page says each element is a separate heap variable and a volatile array reference does NOT make the elements volatile.

options.text: Volatile reads and writes of every element, not the reference
options.says: The page says the volatile modifier applies to the array reference, and the elements stay plain heap variables.

options.text: Volatile reads and writes of the reference, not its elements
options.says: The page says a volatile array reference does not make the elements volatile, and names AtomicIntegerArray for element-level semantics.
